servinfo.title: Front Drive Shaft Assembly Removal and Installation

ptxt.intxrefpoff: Front Drive Shaft Assembly On-Vehicle Inspection:Front

attention2.ptxt: Touching a hot exhaust system component will cause a burn.
Do not perform any service work on the exhaust system until the exhaust system is cool.

s1.ptxt: Hoist vehicle and remove front wheel.
Release caulking (1) from drive shaft nut and remove drive shaft nut (2) with brake pedal depressed.
Remove engine undercover and engine under side covers.
For M/T model, drain transaxle oil.
Disconnect suspension arm joint from steering knuckle.
Disconnect tie-rod end from steering knuckle.
For left side drive shaft assembly, pull out drive shaft joint (1) from transaxle using tire lever (2) or the like.

attention3.ptxt: Turning drive shaft while pulling out drive shaft joint may facilitate release of the circlip fitting of joint spline.

s1.ptxt: For right side drive shaft assembly, remove drive shaft support bracket bolts (1), and then pull out drive shaft joint (2) from transaxle.

servinfosub.title: Installation

attention4.ptxt: Failure to take proper precautions when installing the drive shaft may result in damage to or breakage of the drive shaft assembly.

item.ptxt: Before inserting drive shaft (1), check that there is no foreign material around encoder (2) on wheel hub assembly.
Be careful not to damage the oil seals and boots when installing the drive shaft.
Insert joints only by hand. Never hit joint boots with a hammer.
Check that the differential side joint is fully inserted.
For left side drive shaft assembly, check that the differential side joint circlip is seated in position.

servinfosub.ptxt: Reverse removal procedure noting the following points.

item.ptxt: For left side drive shaft assembly, use new differential side joint circlip.
Apply grease to mating surface of front wheel hub assembly for front drive shaft.
For right side drive shaft assembly (2), install drive shaft support bracket bolts (1) as follows.
Temporarily tighten the bolts in numerical order (“1” – “3”).
Tighten them to specified torque in the same manner as in Step a).
Tighten tie-rod end nut to specified torque.
Tighten suspension arm joint nut to specified torque.
Tighten new drive shaft nut (1) to specified torque.

attention4.ptxt: Once the drive shaft nut is removed, it will no longer have the necessary fastening performance.
Never reuse the drive shaft nut.

item.ptxt: Caulk drive shaft nut as shown.
For M/T model, fill transaxle with oil as specified.
